intro: Today's briefing focuses on the evolving standards for web scraping and AI model training transparency. We also highlight new developments in satellite-based AI and collaborative security efforts between major platforms.

must_know.title: The biggest names in AI are backing a new way to opt out of scraping
must_know.summary: Major AI firms including OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic are adopting a unified 'policy token' signal to respect publisher opt-outs regarding AI data scraping.
must_know.why_it_matters: This industry-wide standard simplifies compliance for publishers, replacing the need for site-by-site configurations.
must_know.update_delta: This is a broader industry adoption of the scraping opt-out signal previously mentioned for OpenAI alone.

must_know.title: Making it easier for websites to express AI training preferences
must_know.summary: OpenAI announced it will support a shared robots.txt-based signal that allows website operators to easily communicate their AI training preferences to multiple AI providers.
must_know.why_it_matters: Standardizing how publishers opt out of AI training could reduce the friction between content creators and AI companies.

must_know.title: OpenAI and Hugging Face partner to address security incident during model evaluation
must_know.summary: OpenAI and Hugging Face have jointly released preliminary findings regarding a security incident that occurred during the evaluation of an AI model.
must_know.why_it_matters: This highlights the growing importance of securing AI model evaluation pipelines against advanced cyber threats.

research.title: Google’s satellite AI server transmits its first response to Earth
research.summary: Google successfully tested an AI-equipped satellite that runs the Gemma 4 model, marking a milestone for edge computing in space.
research.why_it_matters: Demonstrating high-performance AI processing in space could unlock new capabilities for remote sensing and real-time planetary data analysis.
